title: The Department's customer-identifier requirement for monitored dispensing
rule_summary: Under 105 CMR 700.012(A)(3) a pharmacy that dispenses a controlled substance subject to the requirements in 105 CMR 700.012 MUST REQUIRE THAT A CUSTOMER IDENTIFIER IS PRESENTED whenever a controlled substance in Schedules II through V, OR AN ADDITIONAL DRUG, is dispensed. The pharmacy may dispense WITHOUT REVIEWING the customer identifier only if it HAS REASON TO BELIEVE THAT THE FAILURE TO DISPENSE would result in a SERIOUS HARDSHIP for the ultimate user or the ultimate user's agent, AND DOCUMENTS THE REASON; AND the ultimate user or agent PRINTS THEIR NAME AND ADDRESS ON THE REVERSE SIDE OF THE PRESCRIPTION AND SIGNS IT, or, in the case of an electronic prescription, provides an electronic signature; AND the pharmacy provides to the Department those informational fields the Department requires. Under 105 CMR 700.012(A)(4) the Commissioner may waive or modify the requirements in 105 CMR 700.012(A) for a pharmacy to report customer information as the Commissioner specifies. The requirement sits in 105 CMR 700.012, which by 700.012(A)(1) applies to every pharmacy registered with the Commissioner that dispenses pursuant to a prescription a controlled substance in Schedules II through V or one classified by the Department as an additional drug, and by 700.012(A)(2) does not apply to dispensing pursuant to a medication order to an inpatient in a hospital. The Board of Registration in Pharmacy states a customer-identifier requirement of its own in 247 CMR 9.04(14).
exam_relevance: Tests that the customer identifier is required by the Department's monitoring regulation as well as by the Board's practice standards, so an exclusion written for paragraphs of 247 CMR 9.04 does not by itself end the duty for a pharmacy subject to 105 CMR 700.012.

authority.name: Prescription Monitoring Program: pharmacy reporting requirements

exceptions: The documented serious-hardship route, which also requires the recipient's printed name and address on the reverse side of the prescription and their signature, or an electronic signature on an electronic prescription, and the informational fields the Department requires.
A waiver or modification by the Commissioner under 105 CMR 700.012(A)(4).
105 CMR 700.012(A)(2): dispensing pursuant to a medication order to an inpatient in a hospital is outside 105 CMR 700.012 altogether.
common_confusions: Treating the customer identifier as a Board requirement alone, when the Department requires it as well for a pharmacy subject to 105 CMR 700.012.
Reading the hardship route as a judgement call, when it requires a documented reason, the recipient's printed name, address and signature, and the Department's informational fields.
Overlooking that the requirement reaches an additional drug as well as Schedules II through V.
verification_notes: 105 CMR 700.012(A)(1) through (A)(4) read in the official publication of 105 CMR 700.000 on mass.gov on 2026-09-11. Added as a new rule so that no released adjudication is disturbed.
